stories.headline: 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, tsunami threat issued for nine countries in Central and South America
stories.title: 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, tsunami threat issued for nine countries in Central and South America
stories.summary: Panama, Oct 10 : An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 struck off Panama on Friday night. The US Embassy in Panama warned of possible aftershocks and potential tsunami threats across nine countries in Central and South America. In a post shared on X, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said the earthquake occurred at 11:26 pm IST on October 9 at a depth of 10 kilometres. According to the details shared, the epicentre was located 206 kilometres southwest of Panama City, Panama. Meanwhile, the US Embassy in Panama said a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck in La Pitaloza, Panama, at 12:56 local time on October 9, with the location approximately 14 kilometres southwest of Pitaloza Arriba. The embassy warned that aftershocks capable of causing damage may occur. It also said the US Tsunami Warning System had issued potential tsunami threats for Costa Rica, El Salvador, Peru, Mexico, Guatemala, Panama, Nicaragua, Colombia and Ecuador. “Strong and unusual currents and unpredictable surges may occur along the shore,” the embassy said, advising US citizens in the affected areas to stay away from damaged structures and monitor local emergency broadcasts and official guidance for updates. The embassy urged people to avoid damaged areas and refrain from entering damaged buildings. It also advised those near the coast to move to higher ground and follow instructions issued by local authorities. It further warned people to be prepared for possible power and communication outages.

stories.headline: Assam: Flood-Hit Jerenga Pathar Sees Economic Revival Through Thriving Fish Trade
stories.title: Assam: Flood-Hit Jerenga Pathar Sees Economic Revival Through Thriving Fish Trade
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Daily fish harvests of 15-25 quintals boost local trade at flood-hit Jerenga Pathar, with loads of dried indigenous fish transported to Jagiroad.

NAZIRA: Historic Jerenga Pathar, associated with Assam's rich history and the venue of the centenary biennial session of the Axam Xahitya Xabha in 2017, is witnessing a revival of economic activity following the devastating floods of July 19.
The floods left thousands of families in Jerenga Pathar and adjoining areas struggling to rebuild their lives.
For nearly two months, floodwater remained trapped across vast agricultural fields, causing extensive damage to crops and disrupting the livelihoods of farmers.
However, as the water receded, numerous water bodies and pond-like depressions formed across the fields, creating favourable conditions for fish to thrive.
With agricultural activities still affected by the damaged fields, the abundance of fish has opened up an alternative source of income for hundreds of flood-hit families.
According to local sources, around 15 to 20 quintals of fish are being harvested daily from the water bodies.
The growing trade has benefited more than 100 families and provided fresh business opportunities for local traders.

A variety of indigenous and other fish species, including moua, puti, singora, singi, magur, pabho, kawoi, goroi, tura, rohu, borali, mrigal, grass carp and silver carp, are available in the local market.
Fish harvested from Jerenga Pathar is being transported to markets across Sivasagar and Jorhat districts.
Meanwhile, traders are drying indigenous fish on bamboo racks under the sun to cater to the growing market for dried fish.
Large quantities of dried fish are reportedly being transported daily to Jagiroad, known for its major dried-fish market.

stories.headline: Woman Moves Karnataka High Court Seeking LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case
stories.title: Woman Moves Karnataka High Court Seeking LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A woman has approached the Karnataka High Court seeking a direction to the police to initiate the process for issuance of a Look Out Circular (LOC) against her husband, a France-based working professional accused of cruelty and dowry harassment.
The wife contends that her husband remains in India only pending reissuance of his allegedly lost passport and that his departure would prejudice the ongoing investigation.
Advocate Angad Kamath mentioned the matter yesterday before Justice Anant Ramananth Hegde.
The matter is likely to be taken up next week.

The plea challenges an October 8 order of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court rejecting her application under Section 175(3) read with Section 94 BNSS, seeking a direction to the Investigating Officer to request issuance of an LOC and intimate the Regional Passport Officer about the pending criminal case.
"A Look Out Circular opened on the direction sought can be deleted the day this Petition fails; the departure of Accused No. 1 cannot be undone by any order thereafter," the plea states.
The couple married in November 2022.
On September 30, the wife lodged a complaint alleging physical, mental and economic cruelty, unlawful demands for money and retention of her wedding gold.
An FIR was registered under Sections 85, 352 and 351(2) BNS and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
According to the plea, the husband ordinarily resides in France, where he has a valid residence permit, an indefinite-term employment contract and an apartment.
He arrived in India on August 23 and had a confirmed return flight for October 1, but did not board it.
He subsequently reported his passport lost.

stories.headline: When Can ECI Choose Not To Hold Bye-Election? Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Interpretation Of S.151A RP Act
stories.title: When Can ECI Choose Not To Hold Bye-Election? Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Interpretation Of S.151A RP Act
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently reserved judgment on the interpretation of Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which prescribes a six-month period for holding bye-elections to fill casual vacancies in Parliament and State Legislatures, subject to certain exceptions.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Augustine George Masih and Justice Sandeep Mehta reserved the judgment in the Election Commission of India's plea challenging a December 2023 Bombay High Court judgment directing it to hold a bye-election for the Pune Lok Sabha constituency.

Section 151A provides that a bye-election to fill a casual vacancy "shall be held within a period of six months from the date of the occurrence of the vacancy." However, the proviso states that the provision will not apply if "the remainder of the term of a member in relation to a vacancy is less than one year." A further exception applies where the Election Commission, in consultation with the Central Government, certifies that it is difficult to hold the bye-election within the six-month period.
The question is from what point the one-year period under the first exception is to be calculated.
The Bombay High Court held that the relevant date is the date on which the vacancy occurs.
The Pune Lok Sabha seat fell vacant on March 29, 2023 while the term of the 17th Lok Sabha was due to expire over 14 months later on June 16, 2024.
The High Court held that the one-year exception in Section 151A did not apply a bye-election had to be conducted.
The ECI has contended that the six-month period available to the ECI for conducting the bye-election has to be accounted for while determining whether the one-year exception applies.
The issue arose from the vacancy in the Pune Lok Sabha constituency following the death of sitting MP Girish Bapat on March 29, 2023.
The term of the 17th Lok Sabha was due to end on June 16, 2024.
The ECI declined to hold a bye-election, issuing a certificate under Section 151A stating that it was difficult to conduct the election.

It cited, among other reasons, its engagement with elections and preparations for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and the fact that the candidate elected in a bye-election would have only a limited period in office.

stories.headline: "I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes": Trump slams Nobel Committee for awarding Navi Pillay
stories.title: "I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes": Trump slams Nobel Committee for awarding Navi Pillay
stories.summary: Washington, October 10 : US President Donald Trump on Saturday criticised the Norwegian Nobel Committee for awarding the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay, claiming that he deserved the honour for his role in resolving conflicts across the world. In a lengthy post on Truth Social on Friday (local time), Trump questioned Pillay's credentials and accused her of being opposed to Israel, while reiterating his claim that he had settled eight wars and deserved multiple Nobel Peace Prizes. “This is the woman who received the Nobel Peace Prize over the Great United States of America, whose Representative, ME, settled eight Wars, and many other things. I know nothing about this woman, and neither does anyone else!” Trump said. He added, “In fact, to the best of my knowledge, no one ever heard of her other than the fact that she, very obviously, hates Israel.” Trump listed eight conflicts that he claimed to have settled, including Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, Israel and Iran, Egypt and Ethiopia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Israel and Hamas. “I settled 8 Wars, with letters being sent from every President and Prime Minister from the countries that I helped to the Norwegian Nobel Committee, and I’m about to settle, or win, two more, Iran and, Russia/Ukraine,” he said. “Based on my record of PEACE, a record like no one else has ever achieved, I agree! I got back all of the hostages in Israel, including the final 28, both living and dead, and worked with Hamas to do it -- Nobody believed this was possible!” Trump added, while citing his other claimed achievements in international diplomacy and security. He further asserted that he had prevented Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and claimed to have helped avert conflicts in other regions, including tensions involving North Korea, South Korea, Japan, China and Taiwan. “In actuality, I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes, not just 1,” Trump said, referring to the conflicts he claimed to have resolved. The US President also criticised the United Nations, saying it had not helped in resolving the conflicts he cited. “In all of the Wars that I have settled, I never spoke to the United Nations--they were of no help,” he said. “The United States of America, represented by me, as your President, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t. This is an indelible stain on Norway, one that will never be forgotten,” Trump added. He further declared that the Nobel Peace Prize had been “forever discredited by a handful of Radical Ideologues who are Anti-Democracy, and Enemies of Civilization!” Trump's remarks came after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated his support for the US President's Nobel Peace Prize bid. “In recognition of his outstanding contribution, Pakistan had nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize,” Sharif said, adding that he hoped Trump's efforts to promote peace would receive recognition. Meanwhile, the United States announced additional sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday (local time), citing concerns over American sovereignty and the threat posed by the international judicial body. The announcement came on the same day the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Pillay. In a statement, the Norwegian Nobel Committee said Pillay had demonstrated exceptional courage and integrity in advancing a more comprehensive global legal order and had played a significant role in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide were prosecuted. Pillay, a former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, has served as a judge on South Africa's High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory until recently and is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide. In response to the India-Pakistan ceasefire, New Delhi has consistently disputed Trump's claims while remaining steadfast in rejecting any external mediation. India has reiterated that the ceasefire understanding during Operation Sindoor was reached only after Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) reached out to his Indian counterpart to request a halt in military action. India had launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 last year as a decisive, targeted response to destroy terror infrastructure across Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The anti-terror operation was carried out to dismantle terror bases that were utilised to plan the horrific April 22 terrorist attack in Pahalgam. Following effective Indian strikes that dismantled key terror launchpads, the operation was paused on May 10 after a formal request from the Pakistani side. (ANI)

stories.headline: Exclusive | Akash, Isha Ambani take Rs 30,000 crore Jio IPO pitch global; marquee investors seek bigger stake
stories.title: Exclusive | Akash, Isha Ambani take Rs 30,000 crore Jio IPO pitch global; marquee investors seek bigger stake
stories.summary: Jio Platforms Ltd’s planned Rs 30,000 crore initial public offering (IPO) is drawing strong interest from global and domestic investors, with existing marquee backers also seeking to increase their holdings rather than sell, according to people familiar with the matter.The telecom and digital services arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has completed international roadshows across the Americas, Europe and Southeast Asia. Akash Ambani and Isha Ambani have personally met investors across these regions and have been travelling regularly for the roadshows, the people said. Jio is being positioned as a technology company rather than merely a telecom business.The company is now conducting domestic roadshows, where major mutual funds and other institutional investors are seeking a share of the offering. The strong investor response comes as Jio prepares for what could become India’s largest-ever IPO and Reliance Industries’ first public offering in 3 decades.Jio’s existing investor base includes Meta, Google, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, KKR, Vista Equity Partners, Silver Lake, Mubadala, General Atlantic, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and TPG. Meta’s affiliate Jaadhu Holdings is the largest external investor with a 9.98% stake, followed by Google International with 7.73%.Also Read | Jio IPO a 'great responsibility', says Akash Ambani; listing to share value with Indian citizens, including retail investorsNone of these investors plan to sell shares in the mega IPO. In fact, people familiar with the matter said some existing backers are seeking to increase their exposure to Jio Platforms rather than dilute their holdings. The IPO will comprise an entirely fresh issue, without an offer-for-sale (OFS) component.The company is focusing on retail investors and plans to price the IPO in a manner that leaves some value on the table for investors.Jio is set to price its shares at Rs 1,065– Rs 1,119 apiece, according to an earlier report by Bloomberg, which said the company is targeting a market value of as much as Rs 10.3 lakh crore. At the upper end of the price band, the IPO could raise about Rs 30,200 crore, according to Bloomberg calculations.The company plans to open the issue for public subscription on Oct. 21 and close it on Oct. 23. The anchor book is scheduled to open on Oct. 19, with the shares expected to begin trading on Oct. 28. Deliberations are ongoing and details including the price range, valuation and timing could still change.At the proposed valuation, the offering would surpass Hyundai Motor India Ltd’s Rs 27,800 crore IPO in October 2024, currently India’s largest share sale. Jio would also become the first top-three company to list on Indian stock exchanges, according to people familiar with the matter.The valuation is below some earlier expectations. Jio had previously been poised to seek a valuation of about Rs 11 lakh crore. A selloff in Indian stocks has since tempered pricing expectations for several IPOs.Jio filed its draft prospectus in June for an offering of as many as 270 million new shares, equivalent to about 2.93% of its post-issue equity capital. opening: Jio Platforms Ltd’s planned Rs 30,000 crore initial public offering (IPO) is drawing strong interest from global and domestic investors, with existing marquee backers also seeking to increase their holdings rather than sell, according to people familiar with the matter.
The telecom and digital services arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has completed international roadshows across the Americas, Europe and Southeast Asia.
body: Akash Ambani and Isha Ambani have personally met investors across these regions and have been travelling regularly for the roadshows, the people said.
Jio is being positioned as a technology company rather than merely a telecom business.
The company is now conducting domestic roadshows, where major mutual funds and other institutional investors are seeking a share of the offering.
The strong investor response comes as Jio prepares for what could become India’s largest-ever IPO and Reliance Industries’ first public offering in 3 decades.
Jio’s existing investor base includes Meta, Google, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, KKR, Vista Equity Partners, Silver Lake, Mubadala, General Atlantic, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and TPG.
Meta’s affiliate Jaadhu Holdings is the largest external investor with a 9.98% stake, followed by Google International with 7.73%.
None of these investors plan to sell shares in the mega IPO.
In fact, people familiar with the matter said some existing backers are seeking to increase their exposure to Jio Platforms rather than dilute their holdings.
The IPO will comprise an entirely fresh issue, without an offer-for-sale (OFS) component.
The company is focusing on retail investors and plans to price the IPO in a manner that leaves some value on the table for investors.
Jio is set to price its shares at Rs 1,065– Rs 1,119 apiece, according to an earlier report by Bloomberg, which said the company is targeting a market value of as much as Rs 10.3 lakh crore.
At the upper end of the price band, the IPO could raise about Rs 30,200 crore, according to Bloomberg calculations.
The company plans to open the issue for public subscription on Oct. 21 and close it on Oct. 23.
Deliberations are ongoing and details including the price range, valuation and timing could still change.
At the proposed valuation, the offering would surpass Hyundai Motor India Ltd’s Rs 27,800 crore IPO in October 2024, currently India’s largest share sale.
Jio would also become the first top-three company to list on Indian stock exchanges, according to people familiar with the matter.
The valuation is below some earlier expectations.
Jio had previously been poised to seek a valuation of about Rs 11 lakh crore.
A selloff in Indian stocks has since tempered pricing expectations for several IPOs.
Jio filed its draft prospectus in June for an offering of as many as 270 million new shares, equivalent to about 2.93% of its post-issue equity capital.
Motilal Oswal Financial Services estimated Jio’s valuation at Rs 11.2 lakh crore.
Jio has appointed 19 banks to work on the share sale, including Kotak Mahindra Capital Co., Morgan Stanley, Bank of America Corp., Axis Capital Ltd., BNP Paribas SA and Citigroup Inc..

stories.summary: Indian equities staged a sharp rebound on Friday, October 9, bringing an end to the Nifty 50 and Sensex’s eight-week losing streak, with buying across information technology (IT), FMCG, auto and financial stocks lifting benchmark indices.The Nifty 50 gained 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to close at 22,520.45, while the Sensex advanced 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to settle at 72,472.33.However, the rebound comes against a challenging macroeconomic backdrop, with crude oil prices above $100 a barrel, sustained foreign investor outflows, a weaker rupee and tighter monetary policy continuing to weigh on sentiment. With domestic and US inflation data, global bond yields and more corporate earnings in focus, investors will assess whether Friday’s recovery can extend into the coming week.Also read: RBI tightens forex derivative rules: What changes for hedging, cancelled trades Can Nifty bulls sustain the recovery?Analysts remain cautious about the sustainability of the rebound, citing elevated crude prices, foreign investor selling and global macroeconomic uncertainty as key risks. While domestic institutional buying has cushioned the impact of overseas outflows and IT stocks have led Friday’s recovery, the next move will depend on inflation data, global bond yields, oil prices and the September-quarter earnings outlook.Here are the 5 factors that could decide D-Street’s fate next week:1. Crude oil prices and geopolitical tensionsCrude oil prices remain a key macroeconomic concern for Indian equities, with Brent crude trading above the $100-a-barrel mark and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) above $90. Uncertainty surrounding Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and regional energy infrastructure continues to raise concerns over potential supply disruptions, with implications for inflation, the import bill and the rupee."A renewed rise in crude could intensify inflationary pressure, weaken the rupee further and weigh on sectors sensitive to fuel and input costs," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. He noted that a sustained decline in prices would offer meaningful relief to Indian equities by easing concerns over inflation and the country's import bill.Ponmudi added that diplomatic efforts had offered some hope of de-escalation, although the risk of further interruptions to energy shipments remained.Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, CEO of HST Wealth, also flagged elevated oil prices as a risk to the market outlook. He said Brent crude had settled above the $100 mark after trading in a range of roughly $102.50-$105, adding that a sustained decline below $100 would be needed to provide meaningful macroeconomic relief.ALSO READ: Wall Street Week Ahead: Bank earnings, CPI headline busy markets week as S&P 500 hovers near records2. US inflation, bond yields and the rupeeUS inflation and retail-sales data will be important triggers for global markets next week, as stronger readings could keep Treasury yields and the dollar elevated. In India, September consumer price inflation (CPI) and wholesale price inflation (WPI) data, analysts said, will offer cues on domestic price pressures and the potential implications for monetary policy.A stronger-than-expected CPI reading, Hariselvan said, could revive concerns over further Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightening, putting rate-sensitive sectors such as banking, automobiles and real estate under pressure while raising the risk of a broader drag on consumer demand. A softer reading could ease concerns over the eventual peak in interest rates, although relief may prove short-lived if crude prices remain elevated. WPI inflation will provide further indications of how energy and logistics costs are filtering through to producer prices."Global bond yields will remain central to the direction of foreign flows," Ponmudi said. He noted that the US 10-year Treasury yield had eased from its recent peak near 5.36% to around 5.24%, providing some respite for emerging-market assets, although yields remained elevated."Any renewed rise in US yields could strengthen the dollar, increase pressure on the rupee and dampen risk appetite, particularly in rate-sensitive and higher-valued stocks," he said.Hariselvan, meanwhile, said US inflation and retail-sales data would influence the direction of Treasury yields and the dollar. "Stronger-than-expected readings could reinforce expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening, sustaining pressure on emerging-market currencies and foreign portfolio flows," he said. Conversely, softer inflation or signs of moderating consumer demand could pull yields lower and provide Indian equities with a firmer foundation for recovery.The rupee, trading near the Rs 97-per-dollar region, remains vulnerable to high crude prices, elevated US yields and sustained foreign portfolio outflows, according to Ponmudi. He added that a more durable recovery in the currency would likely require greater stability in oil prices and global yields, alongside an improvement in foreign investor flows.The RBI’s policy stance will also remain in focus. Ponmudi noted that the central bank’s October 7 decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shift its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening marked its first rate increase in nearly four years.The move reflected heightened concerns over inflation risks from elevated energy and commodity prices amid global uncertainty. Investors are likely to assess the implications for future policy decisions, borrowing costs and liquidity, with higher interest rates potentially weighing on credit-sensitive sectors and corporate financing conditions.3. FII flows versus domestic institutional buyingForeign investor selling remains a major overhang for the market, although domestic institutional investors have continued to absorb much of the selling pressure. Ponmudi noted that elevated US bond yields could continue to limit overseas allocations to Indian equities, while a renewed rise in yields could strengthen the dollar and put further pressure on the rupee.4. While the restriction does not affect existing H-1B employment, a prolonged freeze could increase localisation and employee-retention costs, he said.5. Technical viewThe Nifty 50 staged a sharp recovery on Friday, ending its eight-week losing streak. The index would need to reclaim and sustain above 23,000 to signal a more meaningful improvement in its short-term technical structure.On the downside, Ponmudi identified 22,400 as the immediate support zone, followed by 22,200 and the psychological 22,000 mark. A break below 22,200 could revive selling pressure and expose the index to lower levels.He noted that momentum indicators had improved from oversold territory following Friday’s rebound. stories.title: Delhi Lockdown: Metro Shutdown, Heavy Security & Airport Detentions Over CEC Gyanesh Kumar Protests
stories.summary: Delhi Lockdown: Metro Shutdown, Heavy Security & Airport Detentions Over CEC Gyanesh Kumar Protests
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A fresh plea in the Supreme Court seeks contempt action over continued Delhi Metro station closures despite its order.
The petition says the restrictions defied judicial directions and disrupted daily life across the capital.

A plea was filed in the Supreme Court on Saturday seeking contempt proceedings against authorities for allegedly violating the court's direction that there should be no "complete prohibition" on the movement of Delhi Metro services and Indian Railways trains to Delhi on October 10 because of the CJP protest.
The petition, filed by Shailendra Mani Tripathi, has made Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan and others respondents.
It alleged that metro stations in the national capital remained shut despite the apex court's October 9 order, and said the restrictions had crippled public life and caused hardship to the public.
The plea referred to the top court's October 9 order, passed while hearing a separate petition against the closure of 57 metro stations and the cancellation of trains to Delhi in view of the protest.
The protest call was given by the Cockroach Janta Party against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

While hearing the matter on Friday, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the Centre to ensure that there was no "complete prohibition" on the movement of metro services and trains coming to Delhi on October 10, saying everything could not be brought to a halt.
The court said that while law enforcement agencies had the right to take steps to restrict unruly movement, citizens should not be unduly harassed.
In its order, the bench said, "It appears that the notifications are overreaching, as they impose a complete ban upon essential public transportation.

Upon our indication that a distinction exists between total 'prohibition' and the 'regulation' of metro and other train movements, Solicitor General of India has fairly agreed to impress upon the authorities to reassess such prohibitions."

The bench also said, "Regarding that assurance, we clarify that although there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of metro trains, a prudent decision may be made to permit the operation of metro trains and other rail services in a suitable and regulated manner." It said such a decision should be widely publicised to prevent further inconvenience.

stories.title: Supreme Court Asks High Court To Re-Hear Plea Against Goa Female Weightlifter's Selection As Coach
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently set aside the Bombay High Court's order, which disallowed Goa weightlifter Vaishnavi S. Ugadekar from selection to the post of Coach (Grade-IV) in Weightlifting.

A bench comprising Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar observed that the High Court decision dismissed the plea without impleading or hearing her, despite her being one of only two candidates competing for the post.
This arose during the selection process where Ugadekar had raised a complaint regarding the fairness of the selection, following which the State Government directed that the tests be re-conducted.
The other candidate filed a writ petition challenging the decision before the High Court, which passed the impugned order without making Ugadekar a party.
The Court has now set aside this order and restored the writ petition for fresh consideration on merits, directing that Ugadekar be impleaded and both candidates be heard.
The Court also directed that its interim order shall continue during the pendency of the writ petition and requested the High Court to decide the matter at the earliest.

It noted: "Considering that the appellant and respondent No. 4 are the only two candidates competing for the post, we deem it appropriate to direct the High Court to decide the matter afresh after affording an opportunity of hearing to both parties.

Consequently, the impugned order is set aside, and the Writ Petition preferred by respondent No. 4 is restored to its original number for a decision afresh on merits upon hearing all parties to the Writ Petition, including the present appellant who shall be impleaded as a party before the High Court."
Further, it has directed that the High Court should decide the matter at the earliest.
The bench has however, clarified that the High Court shall decide the matter afresh on its own merits, uninfluenced by either its earlier order or the Supreme Court's order.

It noted: "Considering that the appellant and respondent No. 4 are the only two candidates competing for the post, we deem it appropriate to direct the High Court to decide the matter afresh after affording an opportunity of hearing to both parties.

Consequently, the impugned order is set aside, and the Writ Petition preferred by respondent No. 4 is restored to its original number for a decision afresh on merits upon hearing all parties to the Writ Petition, including the present appellant who shall be impleaded as a party before the High Court." Further, it has directed that the High Court should decide the matter at the earliest.
The bench has however, clarified that the High Court shall decide the matter afresh on its own merits, uninfluenced by either its earlier order or the Supreme Court's order.
Appearances: For Petitioner(s) Mr. Salvador Santosh Rebello, AOR Ms. Sneha Bhargava, Adv.
